newsitem.title: UK: London gold sharply lower ahead of option expiry.
newsitem.headline: London gold sharply lower ahead of option expiry.

text.p: Precious metals prices were off sharply ahead of the option expiry on Wednesday and some dealers forecast a probe of lower levels before the end of the day.
"The market is very nervous ahead of the option expiry and it is hard to tell where gold is going to be at 14.30 (the expiry time) today. I think it will be between $350-$352," one dealer said.
Gold's rally with silver topped out on Tuesday at around $357.50 when profit-taking came in and a surging dollar and revitalised stock markets encouraged further selling in bullion.
Gold was fixed at $350.15 per ounce, down from $353.70 on Tuesday afternoon and a close of $352.80/$353.30.
In New York the Comex February contract lost $3.30 to close at $354.00 as investors took advantage of the dollar's latest strength and a firmer Dow Jones Industrial Average.
The weakness continued in the Far East, where speculators took profits on higher yen-priced gold futures and the professionals unloaded bullion in arbitrage dealings.
In the Far East added pressure came from South African and Australian producer selling.
"It's been very busy this morning. Gold topped out at $357.50 yesterday then started coming off overnight. It hit some stops at $352.00 and it has been coming down ever since," a dealer said.
Another dealer cited producer and institutional selling as being behind the weakness in Europe. "It could get below $350 before the expiry," he said.
Technical analysts said gold could expect some support at $350 aand then $348, but the next serious support would be at $345.00.
The market's fall over the past 24 hours had left some option writers exposed between $350-$355, which could put pressure on prices closer to the expiry.
Silver effectively gave up its market leadership of the past few days on Tuesday and succumbed to falling gold prices.
It was indicated at $4.92/$4.94, down five cents, having gained 30 cents in the preceding four trading days to briefly touch a high of $5.08.
"Silver already had its move and it's just retracing, " a dealer said.
"It has room to move lower with gold. People had been eyeing strikes at $5.00 but now that it's below they may be looking at $4.85-$4.90," he added.
Platinum was also lower, fixing at a fresh low from September 15, 1993 of $354.00, versus a close of $357.25/$358.25.
